findings.F1: The check failed on Calmar alone (0.686 against 0.75), and the falls behind it come from the weak, frequent part of the signal. In folds B and C the book's deepest fall is -19.5 %, in w16, and w13 (-14.6 %) and w17 (-13.6 %) come next. Over those three falls the held bars lost in every bucket of the day's scaled fall. Bars with z between -1 and -0.5 lost the most (sum -0.675, mean next day -9.8 %, 21 bars).
findings.F2: The gain sits in the strongest case of the signal. Held bars with the day's fall at or below -2.5 of the 30-day swing returned +6.4 % the next day (t 3.4, 27 bars). Bars from -2.5 to -1.5 returned +1.3 % (t 2.4, 109 bars). Bars from -1.5 to 0 returned only +0.3 % to +0.7 % (1062 bars). The top forecast quartile holds 3.55 of the 4.72 summed gain.
findings.F3: Holding only on falls of -1.5 swings or more cuts the deepest fall from -19.5 % to -5.9 %. Calmar rises from 0.83 to 1.31 and Sharpe from 0.97 to 1.01, with a yearly return of 7.7 % against 16.2 %. This is an approximate rebuild at 0.095 % per side.
findings.F4: On agitated bars, a fall of at least 1 swing after a 7-day return below -10 % is followed by +2.29 % excess the next day (t 3.42, 132 cases). The same fall without a prior 7-day decline gives +0.10 % (t 0.21, 161 cases).
findings.F5: The 7-day decline is not an effect of its own, because without the signal it loses. Up days after the same 7-day decline give -1.18 % excess the next day (t -2.24, 186 cases), and small down days give +0.15 % (t 0.26, 222 cases). This fits the brief's theory: forced selling (liquidations, stops, volatility cuts) builds over several down days before it exhausts.
findings.F6: The rebound after a large fall following a 7-day decline lasts two days: +2.48 % excess over 2 days (t 3.24, 132 cases). That is about 13 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F7: Keeping the book only while the coin's 7-day return is below -10 % brings the deepest fall to -10.0 % and Calmar to 1.39, with Sharpe 1.12 and a yearly return of 13.9 %. This is an approximate rebuild.
findings.F8: The effect lives in falling agitated markets.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next day, only while the coin's 7-day return is a fall.
ideas.consequence: Buy a large swing-scaled down day only when it ends a week of decline, and stay out of isolated down days that carry the drawdowns.
ideas.name: agitated fall after weekly decline

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next two days, when the fall ends a 7-day decline.
ideas.consequence: Hold the rebound of a large fall after a week of selling for two days rather than one, so that each trade's move is many times its cost.
ideas.name: two-day rebound after selling

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next day, among falls of more than one and a half times that swing.
ideas.consequence: Trade only the largest swing-scaled falls; the small ones add turnover and drawdown, not gain.
ideas.name: largest scaled falls rebound

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: Buy large swing-scaled falls only while the coin has been falling for the past two months and swinging more than usual, where the forced selling of the theory is concentrated.
ideas.name: falling agitated fall rebound
